full_judgment:
2. This is an application under Article 103 of the Constitution filed challenging the judgment and order dated 23.11.2008 passed in Civil Revision No. 588 of 2002 by the High Court Division making the Rule absolute, thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 31.10.2001 passed in other Appeal No. 25 of 2001 by the learned Joint District Judge (in charge), 1st Court, Nilphamari, and upholding the judgment and decree dated 19.02.2001 passed in Other Class Suit No. 34 of 1998 by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sayedpur, Nilphamari, decreeing the suit declaring that the plaintiffs dismissal order passed by the defendant No.2 communicated vide Memo No. 98/51(7)1(1) dated 05.05.1998 was collusive, void, ineffective, illegal and violative of the Rules of Madrasha Shikkah Board Regulations and the same is not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 4. The trial Court decreed the suit and declared the dismissal order dated 5.5.98 to be invalid, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff, against which the defendants filed Other Class Appeal No. 25 of 2001 in the Court of District Judge, Nilphamari, which on transfer was heard and disposed of by the Joint District Judge (in charge), 1st Court, Nilphamari, allowing the appeal and dismissing the suit after setting aside impugned judgment and decree passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sayedpur, Nilphamari in Other Class Suit No.34 of 1998. 

 6. Being aggrieved the plaintiff moved the High Court Division against the said judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below in Civil Revision No. 588 of 2002, and the High Court Division issued Rule thereon. 

 7. The High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record and submissions of the learned Advocates of the contesting parties made the Rule absolute restoring the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Nilphamari after setting aside those of the appellate Court below observing, amongst others, that the plaintiff was not given opportunity of being heard and that the Madrasha Board did not approve the dismissal order of the plaintiff passed along with the four teachers and that the appellate Court below did not consider the evidence of the plaintiff available on record. 

 9. The learned Advocate submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in not appreciating that the service of the plaintiff respondent No. 1 hereof has been terminated in accordance with law and that there is no necessity of taking any approval from the Appeal and Arbitration Committee of the Madrasha Board for effecting, the dismissal order of the plaintiff. The learned Advocate further submitted that the decree as passed by the Courts below is no executable and bad for defect of parties inasmuch the competent authority namely the Madrasha as well as the Managing Committee of the Madrasha were not made parties and no step was taken in the case to cure the said defect and the High Court Division failed to appreciate this aspect of the case and did not discuss on the finding On this issue as made by the appellate Court below and that the High Court Division erred in not considering the exhibits "Cha" series, which proves service of show cause notice upon the plaintiff and acknowledgement thereof by the plaintiff and hence wrongly observed that the plaintiff was not given any opportunity of being heard and arrived at an erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice, which need be interfered with. 

 "I. For that in the suit the Madrasha was non made, party and thus the suit must fail for want of proper and necessary parties the High Court Division overlooked this point and decreed the suit; 

 II. For that the Court of appeal being last Court of fact upon proper consideration of evidence particularly the letter dated 24.05.1997 and 07.07.1977 found that the plaintiff was very much aware about his dismissal from service as such upon false cause of action filed the suit which cannot be decreed, the High Court Division overlooked this finding of facts and decreed the suit which is liable to be set aside".
